blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
pack_launch_contract.cjs
pack_load_probe.cjs
pack_release_guard.cjs
pack_require_gate.cjs
pack_version_guard.cjs
release_kicker.mjs
release_kicker_guard.cjs
release_packs.mjs
run_with_coverage.js

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
pack_launch_contract.cjs
pack_load_probe.cjs
pack_release_guard.cjs
pack_require_gate.cjs
pack_version_guard.cjs
release_kicker.mjs
release_kicker_guard.cjs
release_packs.mjs
run_with_coverage.js
{"command":"sed -n '60,140p' .github/workflows/quality.yml"}

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

Now let me compare the original and new versions carefully for behaviour differences.

1. `action` early tracker: original `tracker = trackersModule.createTracker(null, (params.jobParams || params).customParams || {})`. New: `var jobParams = params.jobParams || params; var customParams = jobParams.customParams || {}; tracker = trackersModule.createTracker(null, customParams);` — equivalent.

2. Original: `config = configLoader.loadProjectConfig(params.jobParams || params)` — new uses `jobParams`. Equivalent.

3. Missing-result path: original builds comment inline; new uses `handleMissingResult`. Comments identical. Order: partial push → postComment → moveToStatus → remove smTriggerLabel → remove wipLabel. New: pushPartialWorkIfPossible → notifyMissingResult (postComment, moveToStatus) → removeLabelsAfterMissingResult (smTrigger first, then wip). Same order. ✓

4. parseOutcome: original `const status = (result.status || '').toLowerCase();` — new `((result && result.status) || '').toLowerCase()`. Same for result.status. ✓

5. PR failure path: original logs `console.error('PR creation failed — resetting ticket to Backlog for retry')` BEFORE try block; new `resetToBacklogAfterPrFailure` — wait, original comment line: in the original, the console.error comes after `if (!prResult.success || !prUrl) {` and before the try. New: `resetToBacklogAfterPrFailure` logs the same at the start. Same order relative to postComment/moveToStatus? Original: console.error, then try { postComment; moveToStatus }. New: console.error at function start, then try { postComment; moveToStatus }. ✓ Same.

6. Conflict path: original builds conflictComment inline and posts; new `handleConflictingPr` uses buildConflictComment. Check byte-identical: original:
```
'h3. 🚫 Test Automation Blocked — PR Conflicts With Main\n' +
'The test automation branch {code}' + branchName + '{code} still conflicts with {code}' + config.git.baseBranch + '{code} after the agent run.\n' +
'*Pull Request:* ' + prUrl + '\n' +
'A {code}merge_conflicts.md{code} guidance file was present for this run, which means the existing test branch could not be safely auto-aligned with {code}origin/' + config.git.baseBranch + '{code}. ' +
'Do not send this PR into automated review until the branch is deliberately synced with main and only ticket-specific test automation changes remain.\n' +
'Ticket moved to *Blocked* for human conflict resolution.';
```
New buildConflictComment(branchName, baseBranch, prUrl): identical with baseBranch substituted. ✓

7. Git failure path: original `console.warn('Git operations failed:', gitResult.error)` then try { postComment with 'h3. ⚠️ Git Operations Failed\nFailed to commit/push test code: ' + gitResult.error + '\nTicket moved back to *Backlog* — will be re-processed automatically.'; moveToStatus } then removeLabel 'sm_test_automation_triggered'. New resetToBacklogAfterGitFailure identical. ✓

8. Blocked path: new handleBlockedByHuman uses buildBlockedComment. Compare with original: original builds blockedComment; new buildBlockedComment(result, prUrl):
- 'h3. 🚫 Test Automation Blocked — Awaiting Human Setup\n'
- blocked_reason + '\n'
- missing items loop: '* *' + name + '*', ': ' + description, '\n', '{code:bash}' + how_to_add + '{code}\n' — via buildMissingSetupItem: text = '* *' + (item.name || '?') + '*'; if description: text += ': ' + description; text += '\n'; if how_to_add: text += '{code:bash}' + item.how_to_add + '{code}\n'. Identical. ✓
- if prUrl: '\n*Test Branch PR* (test code is ready, skips without credentials): ' + prUrl
- '\nOnce setup is complete, move this ticket back to *Backlog* to trigger re-run.'
✓ identical.

Then order: postComment → moveToStatus → remove WIP → remove SM trigger → console.log('🚫 Test'...). New: same order. ✓ Return `{ success: true, status: 'blocked_by_human', ticketKey, prUrl }` — new: `{ success: true, status: 'blocked_by_human', ticketKey: ticketKey, prUrl: prUrl }`. Same shape. ✓

9. Passed/Failed moves: original inline; new moveToOutcomeStatus with decideTargetStatus. Original log: '✅ Passed — moved', ticketKey, 'to', passedStatus. New: `console.log('✅ ' + outcomeName + ' — moved', ticketKey, 'to', target.statusName);` — outcomeName is 'Passed' or 'Failed'. Identical strings. ✓

10. Final comment: original: `let comment = jiraComment || ''; if (prUrl) comment += '\n*Test Branch PR*: ' + prUrl; if (noCodeChanges) comment += ...`. New buildFinalComment identical. ✓

11. Finalize labels: addLabel AI_TEST_AUTOMATION → remove WIP → remove SM trigger. New finalizeTicketLabels same order. ✓

12. Error catch: buildErrorComment identical. ✓

One subtle difference: In the new `action`, `blockedByHuman` check `if (!blockedByHuman)` after the blocked early-return is now dead code (blockedByHuman always false there since handleBlockedByHuman returns early). Original had the same structure (early return inside `if (blockedByHuman)`), so `if (!blockedByHuman)` was also always true there. Same dead code as original — fine.

Another: new `decideSmTriggerLabel` returns `(customParams && customParams.removeLabel) || null`. Original checks `if (smTriggerLabel)` — null is falsy, so equivalent. But `decideWipLabel` uses `params.metadata` — in the new code the handlers receive `params` and call `postHelpers.decideWipLabel(params.metadata)`. Original computed wipLabel from `params.metadata`. Equivalent. ✓

Edge case: `decideSmTriggerLabel` in `handleMissingResult`'s removeLabelsAfterMissingResult uses `params` — original used `params.jobParams && params.jobParams.customParams && ...removeLabel`. New: `params.jobParams && params.jobParams.customParams` via decideSmTriggerLabel(params). ✓

Edge: what if `params.jobParams` exists but `customParams` is falsy — both handle.

What if `result.status` is non-string, e.g. number? Original: `(result.status || '').toLowerCase()` — a number would throw TypeError. New: `((result && result.status) || '').toLowerCase()` — same behaviour for non-null result. But result could be a non-object? readResultJson returns parsed JSON which could be a string or number (JSON.parse('5')). Original: `result.status` on a number → undefined → `''` OK; on a string primitive, `'abc'.status` → undefined → OK. New: `result && result.status` — same. Equivalent. Actually for `result = 0` or `result = ''` (falsy JSON values) — JSON.parse('0') = 0, falsy → readResultJson returns... original readResultJson: `if (!raw) return null` — raw is '0' truthy string. parsed = 0. `resultBelongsToTicket(0, ticketKey)`: `if (!parsed || typeof parsed !== 'object') return true;` returns true. `console.log('Test result status:', parsed.status)` → undefined. returns 0. Then in action: `if (!result) return handleMissingResult(...)` — 0 is falsy → missing result. New: same, unchanged readResultJson. ✓

Now check `moveToOutcomeStatus` — note it doesn't return anything; original inline code didn't return either. ✓

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
pack_launch_contract.cjs
pack_load_probe.cjs
pack_release_guard.cjs
pack_require_gate.cjs
pack_version_guard.cjs
release_kicker.mjs
release_kicker_guard.cjs
release_packs.mjs
run_with_coverage.js

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

blocks.text:
Now let me compare the original and new versions carefully for behaviour differences.

1. `action` early tracker: original `tracker = trackersModule.createTracker(null, (params.jobParams || params).customParams || {})`. New: `var jobParams = params.jobParams || params; var customParams = jobParams.customParams || {}; tracker = trackersModule.createTracker(null, customParams);` — equivalent.

2. Original: `config = configLoader.loadProjectConfig(params.jobParams || params)` — new uses `jobParams`. Equivalent.

3. Missing-result path: original builds comment inline; new uses `handleMissingResult`. Comments identical. Order: partial push → postComment → moveToStatus → remove smTriggerLabel → remove wipLabel. New: pushPartialWorkIfPossible → notifyMissingResult (postComment, moveToStatus) → removeLabelsAfterMissingResult (smTrigger first, then wip). Same order. ✓

4. parseOutcome: original `const status = (result.status || '').toLowerCase();` — new `((result && result.status) || '').toLowerCase()`. Same for result.status. ✓

5. PR failure path: original logs `console.error('PR creation failed — resetting ticket to Backlog for retry')` BEFORE try block; new `resetToBacklogAfterPrFailure` — wait, original comment line: in the original, the console.error comes after `if (!prResult.success || !prUrl) {` and before the try. New: `resetToBacklogAfterPrFailure` logs the same at the start. Same order relative to postComment/moveToStatus? Original: console.error, then try { postComment; moveToStatus }. New: console.error at function start, then try { postComment; moveToStatus }. ✓ Same.

6. Conflict path: original builds conflictComment inline and posts; new `handleConflictingPr` uses buildConflictComment. Check byte-identical: original:
```
'h3. 🚫 Test Automation Blocked — PR Conflicts With Main\n' +
'The test automation branch {code}' + branchName + '{code} still conflicts with {code}' + config.git.baseBranch + '{code} after the agent run.\n' +
'*Pull Request:* ' + prUrl + '\n' +
'A {code}merge_conflicts.md{code} guidance file was present for this run, which means the existing test branch could not be safely auto-aligned with {code}origin/' + config.git.baseBranch + '{code}. ' +
'Do not send this PR into automated review until the branch is deliberately synced with main and only ticket-specific test automation changes remain.\n' +
'Ticket moved to *Blocked* for human conflict resolution.';
```
New buildConflictComment(branchName, baseBranch, prUrl): identical with baseBranch substituted. ✓

7. Git failure path: original `console.warn('Git operations failed:', gitResult.error)` then try { postComment with 'h3. ⚠️ Git Operations Failed\nFailed to commit/push test code: ' + gitResult.error + '\nTicket moved back to *Backlog* — will be re-processed automatically.'; moveToStatus } then removeLabel 'sm_test_automation_triggered'. New resetToBacklogAfterGitFailure identical. ✓

8. Blocked path: new handleBlockedByHuman uses buildBlockedComment. Compare with original: original builds blockedComment; new buildBlockedComment(result, prUrl):
- 'h3. 🚫 Test Automation Blocked — Awaiting Human Setup\n'
- blocked_reason + '\n'
- missing items loop: '* *' + name + '*', ': ' + description, '\n', '{code:bash}' + how_to_add + '{code}\n' — via buildMissingSetupItem: text = '* *' + (item.name || '?') + '*'; if description: text += ': ' + description; text += '\n'; if how_to_add: text += '{code:bash}' + item.how_to_add + '{code}\n'. Identical. ✓
- if prUrl: '\n*Test Branch PR* (test code is ready, skips without credentials): ' + prUrl
- '\nOnce setup is complete, move this ticket back to *Backlog* to trigger re-run.'
✓ identical.

Then order: postComment → moveToStatus → remove WIP → remove SM trigger → console.log('🚫 Test'...). New: same order. ✓ Return `{ success: true, status: 'blocked_by_human', ticketKey, prUrl }` — new: `{ success: true, status: 'blocked_by_human', ticketKey: ticketKey, prUrl: prUrl }`. Same shape. ✓

9. Passed/Failed moves: original inline; new moveToOutcomeStatus with decideTargetStatus. Original log: '✅ Passed — moved', ticketKey, 'to', passedStatus. New: `console.log('✅ ' + outcomeName + ' — moved', ticketKey, 'to', target.statusName);` — outcomeName is 'Passed' or 'Failed'. Identical strings. ✓

10. Final comment: original: `let comment = jiraComment || ''; if (prUrl) comment += '\n*Test Branch PR*: ' + prUrl; if (noCodeChanges) comment += ...`. New buildFinalComment identical. ✓

11. Finalize labels: addLabel AI_TEST_AUTOMATION → remove WIP → remove SM trigger. New finalizeTicketLabels same order. ✓

12. Error catch: buildErrorComment identical. ✓

One subtle difference: In the new `action`, `blockedByHuman` check `if (!blockedByHuman)` after the blocked early-return is now dead code (blockedByHuman always false there since handleBlockedByHuman returns early). Original had the same structure (early return inside `if (blockedByHuman)`), so `if (!blockedByHuman)` was also always true there. Same dead code as original — fine.

Another: new `decideSmTriggerLabel` returns `(customParams && customParams.removeLabel) || null`. Original checks `if (smTriggerLabel)` — null is falsy, so equivalent. But `decideWipLabel` uses `params.metadata` — in the new code the handlers receive `params` and call `postHelpers.decideWipLabel(params.metadata)`. Original computed wipLabel from `params.metadata`. Equivalent. ✓

Edge case: `decideSmTriggerLabel` in `handleMissingResult`'s removeLabelsAfterMissingResult uses `params` — original used `params.jobParams && params.jobParams.customParams && ...removeLabel`. New: `params.jobParams && params.jobParams.customParams` via decideSmTriggerLabel(params). ✓

Edge: what if `params.jobParams` exists but `customParams` is falsy — both handle.

What if `result.status` is non-string, e.g. number? Original: `(result.status || '').toLowerCase()` — a number would throw TypeError. New: `((result && result.status) || '').toLowerCase()` — same behaviour for non-null result. But result could be a non-object? readResultJson returns parsed JSON which could be a string or number (JSON.parse('5')). Original: `result.status` on a number → undefined → `''` OK; on a string primitive, `'abc'.status` → undefined → OK. New: `result && result.status` — same. Equivalent. Actually for `result = 0` or `result = ''` (falsy JSON values) — JSON.parse('0') = 0, falsy → readResultJson returns... original readResultJson: `if (!raw) return null` — raw is '0' truthy string. parsed = 0. `resultBelongsToTicket(0, ticketKey)`: `if (!parsed || typeof parsed !== 'object') return true;` returns true. `console.log('Test result status:', parsed.status)` → undefined. returns 0. Then in action: `if (!result) return handleMissingResult(...)` — 0 is falsy → missing result. New: same, unchanged readResultJson. ✓

Now, `parseOutcome` is fine.

Now check `moveToOutcomeStatus` — note it doesn't return anything; original inline code didn't return either. ✓

One more difference: original Step 6 else-branch comment. Fine.

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
pack_launch_contract.cjs
pack_load_probe.cjs
pack_release_guard.cjs
pack_require_gate.cjs
pack_version_guard.cjs
release_kicker.mjs
release_kicker_guard.cjs
release_packs.mjs
run_with_coverage.js

blocks.text:
jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
96:        "js/unit-tests/test_agentDocs.js",
120:        "js/unit-tests/test_agentDocsCoverage.js",

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
pack_launch_contract.cjs
pack_load_probe.cjs
pack_release_guard.cjs
pack_require_gate.cjs
pack_version_guard.cjs
release_kicker.mjs
release_kicker_guard.cjs
release_packs.mjs
run_with_coverage.js

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

blocks.text:
name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
96:        "js/unit-tests/test_agentDocs.js",
120:        "js/unit-tests/test_agentDocsCoverage.js",

arguments.command: sed -n '40,80p' .github/workflows/agent-docs.yml

content.text:
- name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."

PR failure path: original logs `console.error('PR creation failed — resetting ticket to Backlog for retry')` BEFORE try block; new `resetToBacklogAfterPrFailure` — wait, original comment line: in the original, the console.error comes after `if (!prResult.success || !prUrl) {` and before the try. New: console.error at function start, then try { postComment; moveToStatus }. ✓ Same.

6. Conflict path: original builds conflictComment inline and posts; new `handleConflictingPr` uses buildConflictComment. Check byte-identical: original:
```
'h3. 🚫 Test Automation Blocked — PR Conflicts With Main\n' +
'The test automation branch {code}' + branchName + '{code} still conflicts with {code}' + config.git.baseBranch + '{code} after the agent run.\n' +

```
New buildConflictComment(branchName, baseBranch, prUrl): identical with baseBranch substituted. ✓

7. Git failure path: original `console.warn('Git operations failed:', gitResult.error)` then try { postComment with 'h3. ⚠️ Git Operations Failed\nFailed to commit/push test code: ' + gitResult.error + '\nTicket moved back to *Backlog* — will be re-processed automatically.'; moveToStatus } then removeLabel 'sm_test_automation_triggered'. - 'h3. 🚫 Test Automation Blocked — Awaiting Human Setup\n'
- blocked_reason + '\n'
- missing items loop: '* *' + name + '*', ': ' + description, '\n', '{code:bash}' + how_to_add + '{code}\n' — via buildMissingSetupItem: text = '* *' + (item.name || '?') + '*'; if description: text += ': ' + description; text += '\n'; if how_to_add: text += '{code:bash}' + item.how_to_add + '{code}\n'. ✓ identical.

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
pack_launch_contract.cjs
pack_load_probe.cjs
pack_release_guard.cjs
pack_require_gate.cjs
pack_version_guard.cjs
release_kicker.mjs
release_kicker_guard.cjs
release_packs.mjs
run_with_coverage.js

      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

3. Missing-result path: original builds comment inline; new uses `handleMissingResult`. Comments identical. Order: partial push → postComment → moveToStatus → remove smTriggerLabel → remove wipLabel. New: pushPartialWorkIfPossible → notifyMissingResult (postComment, moveToStatus) → removeLabelsAfterMissingResult (smTrigger first, then wip). Same order. ✓

4. parseOutcome: original `const status = (result.status || '').toLowerCase();` — new `((result && result.status) || '').toLowerCase()`. Same for result.status. ✓

5. PR failure path: original logs `console.error('PR creation failed — resetting ticket to Backlog for retry')` BEFORE try block; new `resetToBacklogAfterPrFailure` — wait, original comment line: in the original, the console.error comes after `if (!prResult.success || !prUrl) {` and before the try. New: `resetToBacklogAfterPrFailure` logs the same at the start. Same order relative to postComment/moveToStatus? Original: console.error, then try { postComment; moveToStatus }. New: console.error at function start, then try { postComment; moveToStatus }. ✓ Same.

6. Conflict path: original builds conflictComment inline and posts; new `handleConflictingPr` uses buildConflictComment. Check byte-identical: original:
```
'h3. 🚫 Test Automation Blocked — PR Conflicts With Main\n' +
'The test automation branch {code}' + branchName + '{code} still conflicts with {code}' + config.git.baseBranch + '{code} after the agent run.\n' +
'*Pull Request:* ' + prUrl + '\n' +
'A {code}merge_conflicts.md{code} guidance file was present for this run, which means the existing test branch could not be safely auto-aligned with {code}origin/' + config.git.baseBranch + '{code}. ' +
'Do not send this PR into automated review until the branch is deliberately synced with main and only ticket-specific test automation changes remain.\n' +
'Ticket moved to *Blocked* for human conflict resolution.';
```
New buildConflictComment(branchName, baseBranch, prUrl): identical with baseBranch substituted. ✓

7. Git failure path: original `console.warn('Git operations failed:', gitResult.error)` then try { postComment with 'h3. ⚠️ Git Operations Failed\nFailed to commit/push test code: ' + gitResult.error + '\nTicket moved back to *Backlog* — will be re-processed automatically.'; moveToStatus } then removeLabel 'sm_test_automation_triggered'. New resetToBacklogAfterGitFailure identical. ✓

8. Blocked path: new handleBlockedByHuman uses buildBlockedComment. Compare with original: original builds blockedComment; new buildBlockedComment(result, prUrl):
- 'h3. 🚫 Test Automation Blocked — Awaiting Human Setup\n'
- blocked_reason + '\n'
- missing items loop: '* *' + name + '*', ': ' + description, '\n', '{code:bash}' + how_to_add + '{code}\n' — via buildMissingSetupItem: text = '* *' + (item.name || '?') + '*'; if description: text += ': ' + description; text += '\n'; if how_to_add: text += '{code:bash}' + item.how_to_add + '{code}\n'. Identical. ✓
- if prUrl: '\n*Test Branch PR* (test code is ready, skips without credentials): ' + prUrl
- '\nOnce setup is complete, move this ticket back to *Backlog* to trigger re-run.'
✓ identical.

Then order: postComment → moveToStatus → remove WIP → remove SM trigger → console.log('🚫 Test'...). New: same order. ✓ Return `{ success: true, status: 'blocked_by_human', ticketKey, prUrl }` — new: `{ success: true, status: 'blocked_by_human', ticketKey: ticketKey, prUrl: prUrl }`. Same shape. ✓

9. Passed/Failed moves: original inline; new moveToOutcomeStatus with decideTargetStatus. Original log: '✅ Passed — moved', ticketKey, 'to', passedStatus. New: `console.log('✅ ' + outcomeName + ' — moved', ticketKey, 'to', target.statusName);` — outcomeName is 'Passed' or 'Failed'. Identical strings. ✓

10. Final comment: original: `let comment = jiraComment || ''; if (prUrl) comment += '\n*Test Branch PR*: ' + prUrl; if (noCodeChanges) comment += ...`. New buildFinalComment identical. ✓

11. Finalize labels: addLabel AI_TEST_AUTOMATION → remove WIP → remove SM trigger. New finalizeTicketLabels same order. ✓

12. Error catch: buildErrorComment identical. ✓

One subtle difference: In the new `action`, `blockedByHuman` check `if (!blockedByHuman)` after the blocked early-return is now dead code (blockedByHuman always false there since handleBlockedByHuman returns early). Original had the same structure (early return inside `if (blockedByHuman)`), so `if (!blockedByHuman)` was also always true there. Same dead code as original — fine.

Another: new `decideSmTriggerLabel` returns `(customParams && customParams.removeLabel) || null`. Original checks `if (smTriggerLabel)` — null is falsy, so equivalent. But `decideWipLabel` uses `params.metadata` — in the new code the handlers receive `params` and call `postHelpers.decideWipLabel(params.metadata)`. Original computed wipLabel from `params.metadata`. Equivalent. ✓

Edge case: `decideSmTriggerLabel` in `handleMissingResult`'s removeLabelsAfterMissingResult uses `params` — original used `params.jobParams && params.jobParams.customParams && ...removeLabel`. New: `params.jobParams && params.jobParams.customParams` via decideSmTriggerLabel(params). ✓

Edge: what if `params.jobParams` exists but `customParams` is falsy — both handle.

What if `result.status` is non-string, e.g. number? Original: `(result.status || '').toLowerCase()` — a number would throw TypeError. Then in action: `if (!result) return handleMissingResult(...)` — 0 is falsy → missing result. New: same, unchanged readResultJson. ✓

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
pack_launch_contract.cjs
pack_load_probe.cjs
pack_release_guard.cjs
pack_require_gate.cjs
pack_version_guard.cjs
release_kicker.mjs
release_kicker_guard.cjs
release_packs.mjs
run_with_coverage.js

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs

blocks.text:
- name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Install dmtools CLI
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run docs unit tests
        run: |
          dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_agentDocsCoverage.json
